name: UnSub (Siemens S7 PLC targeting) — CISA
brief: A CISA/NSA/FBI/DOE/EPA joint advisory (AA26-231A) warns that unidentified threat actors are conducting persistent reconnaissance and capability development against U.S.-based Siemens S7 Series PLC (S7-200/300/400/1200/1500) installations, using AI-generated exploitation scripts built on the open-source `snap7.dll`/`python-snap7` library and disguised as legitimate OT monitoring tools to gain read/write access to PLC memory, data blocks and ladder logic via S7comm. CISA's own MITRE ATT&CK mapping cites Resource Development → Obtain Capabilities: Artificial Intelligence (T1588.007) for "rapidly iterating exploit code through AI-assisted development." No named actor or nation-state attribution is given, and no confirmed compromise or operational impact is described — CISA frames this as active reconnaissance and pre-positioning, not confirmed intrusion. CISA
ttpMd:
**LLM-aided development** T1587.001 - Develop Capabilities: Malware (AI-generated exploitation scripts)

T1588.007 - Obtain Capabilities: Artificial Intelligence (CISA's own mapping)

T1595 - Active Scanning (Censys/ZoomEye reconnaissance)
